mechanism_narrative: Sustained recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT lifts weekday trips into central shopping areas, so retail and recreation mobility rises over the next four weeks as commuting-linked demand rebuilds.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the previous 4 weeks even when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase or remain stable for four consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stops rising and PARKS remain elevated, discretionary trips shift from home-based outdoor time back toward shopping and leisure venues, pushing RETAIL_REC up within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 8 points while PARKS stays above 15 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL drops below 8 and PARKS remains above 15 for at least one weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharper rebound in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES after a weak baseline signals easing access and fewer movement frictions; retail mobility follows with a one-week lag because shopping trips respond quickly to policy normalization.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 1 point week-on-week while WORKPLACES improves by at least 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week after simultaneous week-on-week gains in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS during summer displaces a share of leisure spending toward outdoor activities, so retail and recreation mobility weakens over the next four weeks as discretionary shopping demand is absorbed by parks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises rather than falls over the next 28 days while PARKS remains elevated or increases further.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps edging upward while RESIDENTIAL stays near its current plateau, routine errand consolidation reduces separate retail outings and keeps RETAIL_REC flat to lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -2 points and RESIDENTIAL remains above 9 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 14 days despite grocery mobility strengthening and residential time staying elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A further narrowing of the gap between TRANSIT and WORKPLACES implies broader return-to-office travel, and that commuting resurgence raises retail visitation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain less negative than -40 and -33 respectively
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not move upward over 28 days while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both stay in their recovery ranges.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT stays deeply suppressed but WORKPLACES stop falling, people still commute less than they work, and the missing travel demand keeps retail and recreation mobility below the previous four-week average.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -40 and WORKPLACES remain below -30
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the next week even though TRANSIT stays below -40 and WORKPLACES stay below -30.

mechanism_narrative: In summer, a continued rise in PARKS combined with a stable positive RESIDENTIAL baseline diverts time away from enclosed shopping, so retail mobility weakens over a one-month horizon.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above 20 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining above 20 and RESIDENTIAL remaining above 9.
